output.brief:
The wrong expiry dates were not caused by the agency operators or the printer firmware. Printer job records show that from 4 Oct the line integration service was already sending a 36-month shelf life for Veltranol, and the printer printed exactly that. No operator overrides were made. Earlier jobs, including those after the firmware change and those run by agency operators, were correct. On 3 Oct Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value in the ERP, valid only from March 2027. The integration service appears to have used it early, which contradicts the vendor's statement. Why it did so is still unconfirmed. Two Veltranol lots on Line 1 are affected as well, and they are in the warehouse. The camera only checks the print against the job data, so it could not catch the error.

Do not issue warnings or remove the operators. Reset the Veltranol shelf-life record so only the approved 24-month value can be read. Extend the hold to every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two on Line 1. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Check retained cartons of the two other products with future-dated edits (HX-15-30, MR-05-14). Ask the vendor and IT why a future-dated value was sent. Keep the camera check switched on. I'm fairly confident, but the mechanism and the other products are not yet verified.
